changelog: THE ENEMY TELEGRAPHS ITS NEXT MOVE. Turn on Danger and every enemy shows a ghost on the tile it is heading for, an arrow to what it will strike, and the damage it will deal — summed per victim, so three enemies converging on one unit read as the one number that decides your turn. It is driven by the AI that actually runs, so what you are shown and what lands cannot drift apart, and it covers every actor on the field: the faction AI, turrets, raiders, mire gators and the roaming enemy HQ. DANGER IS NOW TWO LAYERS, TOGGLED SEPARATELY AND REMEMBERED. Threat range shades everything the enemy can hit, and in deeper red the tiles they can move onto and fire from — the ground worth taking or blocking first. Enemy intent is the ghosts and the arrows. Either can be turned off without losing the other. MOVEMENT STOPS AT THE EDGE OF THE FOG: you may push one tile into the unknown, but your army will no longer march blind three tiles deep into ground it has never seen. THE GAME NOW TEACHES ITSELF — coaching went from 4 tips to 22, each bound to the action that earns it. THE GAME HAS SOUND: 42 effects and layered music beds, with a separate desperate layer for boss fights. This is the first Mac build since 0.0.38, so it also brings everything from 0.0.39 through 0.0.43 — the desktop pass over the overlays, map and battle HUD, the map bar rebuild, the upgrade and card-change reveals, and the Daily Commission. Still universal and still notarized: one download runs natively on Intel and Apple Silicon, and opens with no Gatekeeper warning.
